title: Choose Workbench's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Exhibition. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Exhibition
options.lineage: Museum hangs: white walls, vinyl wall text, tombstone labels beside each work
options.thesis: Every prompt hangs like a work in a show, its wall label explaining how it was made.
options.viewport: Today's hang: three works on one shared centreline, each with a tombstone label (model as medium, creator, source); a deep-blue feature wall carries the exhibition title and the three rooms: Prompts, Repos, Guides.
options.risk: Can read hushed and precious if the labels are timid; the rooms must feel browsable, not roped off.

raised.raise: Every work hangs on one measured centreline grid, so a wall of mixed aspect ratios still reads as one calm row.
The whole hang is walkable by keyboard: arrow keys move work to work, Enter opens the label.
Focus is lighting: the work you approach gets the spotlight, the rest of the wall dims a step.
The show is dated: each day's refresh is announced as a new hang with its opening date on the wall.

options.label: The Contact Sheet
options.lineage: Darkroom contact sheets marked up in red china marker
options.thesis: Prompts are proofed like film: frames on a sheet, the good ones circled and annotated in grease pencil.
options.viewport: A black contact sheet of today's images in film strips; one frame circled in red with its prompt marked up phrase by phrase in the margin.
options.risk: Photography-darkroom is a familiar creative trope, and dense black sheets can feel heavy for the repo directory.

options.label: Video Store Wall
options.thesis: Aisles are types of work; every repo and prompt is a box you pull off the shelf.
options.viewport: A Design aisle header over a shelf of repo spines, one pulled face-out with a handwritten staff-pick talker.
options.case: Genre aisles map cleanly onto 'type of work'; loses on the image gallery, where prompts are not boxes.
options.risk: Nostalgia can overpower content; spines are hard to read for long repo names.

options.label: Memphis Showroom
options.thesis: A playful showroom where each prompt role is its own shape and pattern.
options.viewport: Images set on pattern-filled plinths, prompt roles as toy-like shapes, a yellow pressed control.
options.case: Designers identify with it strongly; loses on clarity once 600 repos need scanning.
options.risk: Pattern noise competes with the images it is meant to frame.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscopes on a signal bench
options.thesis: Star growth as a phosphor trace on a graticule.
options.viewport: A rising-repos trace with knobs for category and timebase.
options.case: Non-coder creators don't recognise a signal bench; prompts lose their images.
options.kept: Everything measured against one grid: works hang on a shared centreline.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The library as a 2 a.m. text board.
options.viewport: A title screen with numbered menu exits.
options.case: A text grid cannot show the images that lead the gallery.
options.kept: Complete keyboard operation across the hang.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Content glows awake as you approach.
options.viewport: Prompts bloom along a glowing vein network.
options.case: Beautiful but hides the filters creators need.
options.kept: Focus as light: the approached work is spotlit.

options.label: Rain-Night City
options.thesis: The library as a city whose lights change by the hour.
options.viewport: A skyline where each window is a repo.
options.case: No natural home for prompt anatomy.
options.kept: Time as state: each daily refresh is a dated new hang.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean gallery-and-directory site like Lexica or PromptHero, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar over a masonry grid of images, filter pills above, a sidebar of models.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every prompt gallery by design.
